messages.author: 5e53516a6295cc09
messages.subject: Asymmetric component in bilat.symmetry
parts:
Dear colleagues,

I'm working with geometric morphometric analysis of symmetry of skull data. Dealing with bilat.symmetry() I have found the following issue when we have object symmetry. The function computes asymmetric component by subtracting symmetric component from the first n landmark configurations of the dataset (where n is the number of specimens). It is OK when there are only one replicate per specimen. But when there are several replicates we can get problems when replicates are follow one by one (eg, 1 1 2 2 3 3 etc). In my opinion, in the case of multiple replicates asymmetric component should be computed as differece between average of replicates and symmetric component.
This is not a great issue because there are no such problems with matching symmetry and DA- and FA-components of asymmetry. But I spent a bunch of time this week disentangling algorithmic details of implementation.
Specifically, I discuss lines 285-286 of the bilat.symmetry.r file:
    asymm.component <-simplify2array(lapply(1:n.ind, function(j)
    {mn.shape + A[,,j] - symm.component[,,j]}))


Best regards,
Basil Yakimov,
Lobachevski State University of Nizhni Novgorod

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Asymmetric component in bilat.symmetry
parts:
Dear Basil, and others,

I wish to respond to your inquiry.  The bilat.symmetry function did indeed have some legacy code that did not make sense.  We had code for computing the difference between subjects, averaged over replicates - as you intuited - but only applied it to matching symmetry (and it eludes us why or how we missed it on object symmetry).  The fix was simple - just had to remove the condition for matching or object symmetry (which only implicates the set-up for the shape analyses, but not the analyses, themselves); however, we wanted to test the function a bit before sending the updates to our stable version of the software on GIthub.  We have done that now - sorry for the delay and inconvenience.

Thanks for bringing the issue to our attention!

Mike
